post_title: How many new suspected measles cases will Bangladesh's DGHS report for the 24 hours to 8:00 am on 13 November 2026?

question.title: How many new suspected measles cases will Bangladesh's DGHS report for the 24 hours to 8:00 am on 13 November 2026?
question.description:
Bangladesh has been in the grip of its largest measles outbreak on record since 15 March 2026, when the outbreak came to official attention; it is the largest measles outbreak anywhere in the world in 2026, with roughly 227,000 suspected cases and 1,251 deaths reported by late October. The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia's Epidemiological Bulletin (21 October 2026) reported that approximately 1,000–1,300 suspected cases have been reported daily since early September "with no steady decline", and that ISO week 42 (12–18 October) saw 8,216 suspected cases, 701 confirmed cases and seven suspected deaths.

The DGHS control room issues a daily measles bulletin ("হাম প্রেস রিলিজ"), normally in the afternoon local time, covering the 24 hours to 8:00 am that day; Bangladeshi outlets (The Business Standard, The Daily Star, Daily Sun, RTV, Bangladesh Post, Sarabangla) report its figures each day. The bulletin gives new suspected cases, new laboratory-confirmed cases, hospital admissions and deaths for the preceding 24 hours, plus cumulative totals since 15 March. Recent daily counts of newly identified suspected cases: 1,232 (bulletin of 27 October), 1,322 (28 October), 1,251 (29 October), 1,316 (30 October). The 30 October bulletin put cumulative suspected cases at 227,673, cumulative confirmed cases at 23,770, suspected measles deaths at 1,146 and confirmed measles deaths at 105 (1,251 combined), with 202,639 suspected-case hospital admissions since March. Cumulative suspected cases were 208,570 on 14 October and 213,244 on 18 October. Note that media reports frequently quote the combined suspected-plus-confirmed daily figure — e.g. on 29 October the combined figure was reported as 1,315 while the suspected-only count was 1,251 — so secondary coverage must be read carefully.

An independent review of the national immunisation programme (Expanded Programme on Immunization) and vaccine-preventable disease surveillance, supported by WHO and partners and conducted 4–14 October 2026, found that only 82% of children were fully immunised against a 95% target and that around 40% of vaccinator posts were vacant. Its report was submitted to the government in late October and seen by AFP on 26 October, warning that diphtheria, whooping cough and polio outbreaks could follow; the health ministry said it would work towards implementing the recommendations. A nationwide measles–rubella vaccination campaign targeting roughly 3.4 million unvaccinated and missed children began on 26 September 2026.

Because the daily figure counts suspected (clinically compatible, not necessarily laboratory-confirmed) cases and reflects day-to-day variation in reporting and verification, single-day totals fluctuate by roughly ±10% around the prevailing trend even when the epidemic curve is flat or slowly declining, which is what makes the count for one specific 24-hour window genuinely uncertain.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves using the DGHS (Directorate General of Health Services, Bangladesh) daily measles bulletin — published in Bengali as "হাম প্রেস রিলিজ" — covering the 24 hours from 8:00 am Bangladesh Standard Time (UTC+6) on 12 November 2026 to 8:00 am on 13 November 2026, which is listed at https://dghs.gov.bd/pages/press-releases (mirrored at https://dghs.gov.bd/pages/news). The resolved value is the bulletin's 24-hour figure for newly identified suspected measles cases (patients with measles-like symptoms) — i.e. the suspected-case line, not the combined suspected-plus-confirmed figure, not laboratory-confirmed cases alone, and not hospital admissions; a value of 1,300 new suspected cases resolves as 1,300. If the bulletin's 24-hour suspected figure cannot be obtained, the value is instead computed as the cumulative suspected-case total reported in the bulletin dated 13 November 2026 minus that reported in the bulletin dated 12 November 2026. If the DGHS bulletin itself cannot be accessed or read at all, the value as reported for that same bulletin by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: The bulletin is normally released in the afternoon (local time) of the date it covers; if the 13 November 2026 bulletin is delayed, resolution waits for it rather than annulling. The resolved value is the figure as first published for that bulletin, and any later upward or downward revision by DGHS of that day's count does not change the resolution. If no DGHS bulletin covering a period ending 8:00 am on 13 November 2026 (and no reporting of one) exists at all, the question is annulled.
